Strong experience with surgical workflows and pre-admission processes
Minimum 5 years in utilization management, case management, or perioperative services.

The Presurgical Utilization Manager is responsible for overseeing preoperative utilization review processes to ensure accurate patient status designation (Inpatient vs. Outpatient/Observation) prior to surgery. This role partners closely with surgeons, anesthesia leadership, scheduling teams, and case management to optimize clinical appropriateness, regulatory compliance, and financial stewardship. The role ensures that all surgical patients are assigned the correct admission status based on clinical criteria, payer requirements, and organizational protocols—minimizing denials, ensuring compliance, and supporting appropriate resource utilization.
Computer literacy and proficiency
Analytical mindset with focus on denial prevention and a high attention to detail and compliance.
Strong physician engagement and influence skills as well as the ability to work cross-functionally (surgery, anesthesia, revenue cycle, case management)
Knowledge of University policies and procedures.
Must possess the skill, knowledge, and ability essential to the successful performance of assigned duties
Must demonstrate customer service skills appropriate to the job

Knowledge of standard office equipment (i.e., calculator, fax, photocopier) and personal computer and computer software skills (i.e., MS Windows, Excel, Access, Word, PowerPoint, internet, e-mail). Windows computer skills including proficient use of keyboarding, use of mouse or keys for functions such as selecting items, use of drop-down menus, scroll bars, opening folders, copying and similar operations required upon employment or within the 1st two weeks of employment to perform the essential functions of the job
Familiarity with CMS rules, InterQual and/or Milliman criteria
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English
Deep knowledge of inpatient vs. outpatient regulatory requirements
Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and maintain a work pace appropriate to the workload
